db_evidence.notes: The Shanghai clue (total_intervals second window, 162,568-162,621s) is exactly and cleanly retrievable: episodes:30sec:005423/005424 textually describe a man in a black suit pulling a saxophone from a case and playing for the crowd, matching the reference almost verbatim. The Changsha clue (total_intervals first window, 331,372-331,388s) does NOT match any 'Sunshine Rainbow Little White Horse' or saxophone content in the DB at that exact offset -- that window instead covers an unrelated fortune-telling/palm-reading street scene. The actual 'ishowspeed sings his sunshine and rainbow song' episode row is at 336,672-336,702s (episodes:30sec:011229), about 5,300s away from the given total_intervals window, and a separate Changsha street scene with an actual saxophonist exists near 248,126-248,380s but plays a different song ('Careless Whisper' per clip_qa in rollout-3). None of this affected outcomes because the decisive evidence for the correct answer was the Shanghai window, which every rollout located reliably; the Changsha side only needed to be ruled out, and all 5 rollouts did so (via text absence of 'saxophone' near the stage-singing row, or via clip_qa song-title mismatch).

root_causes: Not applicable in the failure sense -- all 5 rollouts scored 5/5. The Shanghai saxophone scene has a highly distinctive, easily-embedded textual description ('pulls a saxophone from case and plays for a crowd') that semantic_search over episodes reliably surfaces within a handful of queries.

The Changsha side of the question is genuinely ambiguous in the source data (a stage vocal performance of the target song vs. a separate street saxophone ensemble playing a different song), but every rollout independently disambiguated correctly, either by absence of 'saxophone' text near the stage-singing episode row or by clip_qa confirming the street saxophonist's song was not the target.
what_worked: Iterative semantic_search with query reformulation (e.g. 'street musician saxophone Shanghai trip' vs '...Changsha trip') efficiently split the two candidate locations and let the agent compare them side by side.

run_sql on the surrounding 30-second episode rows around a semantic_search hit gave a precise, quotable time window and confirmatory detail (color of saxophone, clothing, dancing streamer) matching the reference answer almost verbatim.

In the one rollout that used clip_qa (rollout-03), the visual sub-agent correctly avoided being fooled by the confounding Changsha saxophone-plus-wrong-song scene by identifying the song title, giving a stronger disambiguation signal than text search alone.
All rollouts converged on the same evidence (episodes:30sec:005423/005424, ~162,558-162,618s) despite different search paths, indicating this fact is robustly indexed and retrievable in the DB.
transferable_lessons: For 'which of two similar-seeming locations has property X' questions, run the same targeted semantic_search query once per candidate location/trip in parallel rather than a single broad query -- this pattern (seen in rollouts 1, 2, 4) cleanly separates confounds.

When two candidate scenes both plausibly match a generic feature (e.g. 'saxophone present'), use clip_qa or SQL text to check the more specific distinguishing feature (song title) rather than stopping at the first shared attribute -- rollout-03 demonstrates this correctly resolves scenes that could otherwise cause a wrong answer.

A temporal_certificate of 'Ultra-Long' and disjoint total_intervals across a whole month timeline still converged reliably here because the target scene had unusually distinctive, literal caption text ('pulls a saxophone from case'); such literal-description scenes are easy wins for semantic_search regardless of the huge timeline span.
open_questions: Why does the question's total_intervals[0] (331,372-331,388s, Changsha) not correspond to any 'Sunshine Rainbow Little White Horse' or saxophone content in the DB, while the actual matching stage-singing episode row sits ~5,300s later at 336,672-336,702s? This looks like a benchmark/clue-interval alignment issue upstream of the agent, though it did not affect any rollout's score here.
